rhythm.value: 19 judged shots in 8.67 s (detector 11): 18 cuts, 124.6 cuts a minute, median shot 0.134 s, but the median hides the shape. Three tempos in sequence: (1) hook 0-1.133 s, a 9-frame strobe and a 25-frame plate; (2) two long breaths, 44 and 28 frames (1.133-3.533); (3) a burst of ten 4-frame plates (3.833-5.167, exactly 0.1333 s each) after a 9-frame lead-in, then a 6-frame plate; (4) an emptying ending of 6, 9, 50 and 40 frames. Shot lengths p10 0.133 s, p90 1.467 s (variety about 11x). Captions (5) carry their own clock, independent of cuts: 30, 19, 28, 54 and 34 frames on screen, each entering and leaving in one frame, and none during the two breath plates' first halves or the second half of the burst. Sound, unheard (I cannot hear the film): onsets run at 4.27 a second (1.28 per 0.3 s), so onset ratios say nothing. On the 18 judged cuts 7 land within 80 ms of a beat (0.39) against 0.314 by chance, 10 on onsets (0.56) against 0.631, 1 within a frame of a downbeat against 0.039: all chance. Tempo confidence 0.164 at 127.6 BPM while audiomap reads 163 BPM at 0.32, so there is no grid. The detector's own sync.json (0.40 vs 0.314, 0.70 vs 0.631) is also chance. What the 50 ms RMS does show (read after seeing the curve, so suggestive only, confidence about 0.5): loudness comes in bursts with troughs near -30 dB at 1.20-2.10, 2.80-3.55 and 4.40-4.90 s, and the bursts match the captions' on and off times (on 0.133/2.067/3.533 against rises at 0.35/2.15/3.60; off 1.133/2.700/4.467 against falls at 1.15/2.75/4.40). The bursts are most likely the voiceover, and each caption arrives about 2 frames (once 6) before its spoken line. The two long holds sit between lines. From 4.95 s the level climbs to -5 dB at 7.9 s while the picture empties, and the film ends on black under loud sound, not silence.

value.name: flash-montage-under-continuous-caption
value.description: One caption holds frame-centre while plates change under it: 9-frame lead plate (F106-F114), then eleven cuts on exact 4-frame steps at F115, F119, F123, F127, F131, F135, F139, F143, F147, F151, F155 (3.833-5.167 s): ten 4-frame plates, then a last plate held 6 frames. The caption stays on the lead plate and the next five (to F134), is absent for five (F135-F153), and the next line appears on F154 and holds over the 6-frame plate. Plates alternate subject and grade (black, dome, sparks, eye callback, wireframe, glass, particles, hand, droplet, digits, drawing); the eye plate is the hook's eye, a callback. Same move in short at the hook: the first caption holds F4-F33 across the ring strobe, the white-out and the eye.
value.why: The caption is the fixed point the eye holds, so 0.13 s plates are read as a list of possibilities rather than as noise; exact 4-frame steps make the burst feel mechanical and deliberate, and the callback plate ties the surge back to the opening image.

value.name: grade-step-on-held-plate
value.description: A held plate exits through hard grade steps rather than a cut effect: crescent teal (F70), monochrome high-contrast (F71-F73, 3 frames), negative black-on-white (F74-F75, 2 frames), cream with a brown crescent and RGB fringing (F76-F77, 2 frames), then the next plate enters in negative for 1 frame (F78) before its own sepia grade (F79). Other instances: the eye grades in from white (F9) through magenta (F14-F15) to teal (F16); the pen jumps to a bright neutral grade at F100; the burst's eye goes monochrome on F130; the caption card goes ultramarine to navy at F165.
value.why: Each step is a full-frame change of luminance or polarity, which the eye reads as a hit without any movement; using 1-3 frame grades as the transition keeps the subject in place so the change is felt, not followed, and it makes footage look authored.

value.name: blinking-caret-line-swap
value.description: On a black ground with a faint soft card (#0C0F0C), a thin vertical caret with a green-white bloom stands through the middle of the centred line. It blinks on a 19-frame cycle: on F170-F179 (10), off F180-F188 (9), on F189-F197 (9), a 1-frame break-up into fragments at F198, off F199-F207, on F208-F215 (8). On F208 the whole line is removed in one frame, leaving the caret alone; the caret goes at F216; four empty frames (F216-F219); the next line appears whole at F220 (7.333).
value.why: A caret is the universal sign for 'being written', so the line reads as a draft; deleting it whole and replacing it after four empty frames makes the last line land as a correction of the previous one, which is the film's argument.

value.name: frame-strobe-graphic-open
value.description: The film opens on a dot-matrix ring (about 0.55 of frame height, centred) alternating with black on single frames: ring F0, black F1-F2, ring with a blue vertical bar F3, black with bar and caption F4, dim ring F5, black F6, ring on ultramarine #062477 F7-F8, then a full white frame F9 that becomes the first plate. The caption is on from F4 and does not flicker.
value.why: Single-frame alternation is the strongest attention signal available in the first 0.3 s; holding the caption steady through it makes the words the stable thing to read.

value.name: slow-push-macro-hold
value.description: Two long, near-still macro plates after the hook: the crescent holds 44 frames with a 7.2% linear push (motion.json s004: z 0.0696, span90 1.03 s, fit 'none', cut off by the grade exit) and the caption arrives only after 28 frames (F62); the pen nib holds 28 frames with a 2.8 degree clockwise roll and 2% push (s007: power2.in, span90 0.59 s). Both sit in the quietest stretches of the soundtrack (50 ms RMS about -30 dB at 1.20-2.10 s and 2.80-3.55 s against -10 to -15 dB in the bursts), which are most likely the gaps between spoken lines (inferred).
value.why: After a 1.1 s hook of strobe and annotation, the viewer needs a rest; long holds with almost no motion and almost no sound make the following 4-frame burst feel faster than it is.

evidence: RMS 50 ms of media/source.mp4 (computed in scratch)

value.note: 0.233 s (F7) is not a new shot: the same ASCII dot ring, same size and centre, flips from white-on-black to white-on-ultramarine. F0-F8 are one ring strobing frame by frame (ring, black, ring, black with a blue bar, ring, black, ultramarine ring x2). Grade or polarity steps on one held element are counted inside the shot throughout this analysis.

The real cut is at F9 (0.300): a full white frame that is the macro eye plate over-exposed. Contrast-boosted F12-F13 show lash and iris structure under the white, and the HUD boxes drawing on F10-F13 sit at exactly the positions they hold over the visible eye from F14.

0.467 s (F14, detector 'match' 0.45) is the same eye plate graded down from white to magenta (F14-F15), then to teal at F16 (0.533). HUD layer unchanged across F13/F14. Merged into the eye shot that starts at 0.300.

2.367 s (F71, teal to monochrome white) and 2.467 s (F74, polarity inverted: black crescent on white, 2 frames) are grade steps on the same light-crescent plate; a third step to cream with a brown crescent and RGB fringing follows at F76 (2.533). Same framing throughout; the crescent never moves between grades.
3.333 s (F100, detector 'match') is an exposure/grade step on the same pen-nib plate: sepia-cream to bright neutral grey, nib and line unchanged.
